A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fair Kernel Decomposition work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the new Appendix D in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original fairness–accuracy evaluations on three datasets, plus experiments on multiple protected attributes, regularization sensitivity, and Nystroem approximation.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds linear-removal comparisons and appendix experiments with additional neural baselines and model sizes.

M1.justification: The ridge-based null-space procedure, kernel transformation, out-of-sample application, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. The correction to Equation (6) aligns the weight-vector orientation with the existing objective and proof; it does not establish a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Communities & Crimes, Montana ACSIncome, and Montana ACSTravelTime with the same targets and protected attributes, including the multiple-attribute Crimes scenario. The added experiments reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially extends the comparisons by evaluating linear null-space removal followed by kernel SVR, labeled SVR-INPL, in Section 4.4 and Kong et al.'s NN-FREM in Appendix D. The original Figure 1 comparator set, including KRR-FKL, NN-HGR, and the dummy predictor, is retained.

E3.justification: The new linear-removal experiment introduces separate iteration grids, reaching 200 iterations for SVR-INPL and 140 for SVR-FKD. Appendix D also tests NN-HGR with hidden widths 250 and 230 instead of 100 and 80. The existing benchmark metrics and five-fold cross-validation design are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds a direct test of the central kernelization choice by comparing nonlinear feature-space removal with linear removal on ACSIncome. Appendix D adds a neural-network capacity check across the retained datasets. These extend the validation beyond v1's multiple-attribute, regularization, and approximation analyses, which remain present.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-fold cross-validation and empirical standard deviations as error bars. The added plots follow the existing reporting practice; no new seed information, repeated-run scheme, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: New Figures 3 and 5 substantially expand the reported fairness–accuracy results. Figure 3 shows linear removal reaching a fairness plateau while SVR-FKD continues improving fairness; Appendix D reports NN-FREM as less competitive than KRR-FKL and no overall benefit from the larger NN-HGR configuration under the tested settings. The original Nystroem results are retained as Figure 4.

T1.justification: Equation (6) corrects the transpose orientation of the ridge solution. Appendix A.2 newly makes the invertibility requirement for the multiple-attribute normalization explicit and identifies linearly dependent protected attributes as a problematic case. The principal theoretical results and remaining proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: kernel-space null-space removal, preservation of kernel properties, out-of-sample extension, model and fairness-score agnosticism, and competitive regression performance. The revised abstract's emphasis on the empirical feature space makes an existing contribution more explicit.

C2.justification: v2 explains linear-removal saturation through residual nonlinear dependence and states when linear removal suffices. It replaces the emphasis on fairness-metric computation as a scalability obstacle with the method's quadratic storage limitation and discusses further kernel approximations. It also drops the ACSTravelTime 'without harming performance' characterization and adds a specific misuse caveat in the Impact Statement.

D1.justification: Table A.1 newly discloses 500 training epochs for NN-HGR; v1 states no epoch count. Appendix D supplies NN-FREM hyperparameters and the larger NN-HGR topology, while Section 4.4 documents the new comparison's iteration grids. Both versions provide the same code-access pointer.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of Kong et al. (2025), Lai and Guan (2025), Ravfogel et al. (2022), and Grünewälder and Khaleghi (2021), including distinctions from prior kernel-based information removal. It adds Rahimi and Recht (2007) for future approximation work and removes the Kernel PCA reference. This expands context without redefining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 refines the abstract, consolidates contribution bullets, and makes grammar and terminology corrections throughout. It adds Section 4.4, Appendix D, acknowledgements, and an Impact Statement while retaining the main section order and most existing prose.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel linear comparison and nine-panel appendix comparison using the existing plotting style. Retained figures are resized, and the Nystroem plot moves from Figure 3 to Figure 4 with revised tick spacing and caption details. Table A.1 gains an epoch-information line; the overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The previously absent linear-removal control and Appendix D comparisons strengthen evidence for kernelization and check neural-baseline capacity. The equation correction, explicit invertibility and storage limitations, and epoch disclosure improve precision and transparency. These are useful but bounded gains within the existing method and dataset coverage.
